subsystems.name: Brain mapping
subsystems.role: records the wiring diagram — which neuron connects to which, and how strongly.

subsystems.name: Activity recording
subsystems.role: captures what the brain is doing, not just how it is wired.

subsystems.name: Cell and synapse models
subsystems.role: mathematical rules for how each neuron and connection behaves.

subsystems.name: Emulation compute
subsystems.role: the hardware that would run a brain-sized simulation.

subsystems.name: Simulation software
subsystems.role: turns the model into a running, behaving system.

subsystems.name: Embodiment and interface
subsystems.role: gives the emulated mind senses and the ability to act.

buildSteps.title: Map a complete small brain
buildSteps.detail: Serial electron microscopy and machine-learning image analysis have produced the full connectome of the nematode Caenorhabditis elegans (302 neurons, first published in 1986) and, in 2024, the adult fruit fly's roughly 140,000 neurons.

buildSteps.title: Map a mammalian cortex
buildSteps.detail: Denser tissue needs better staining, faster imaging and vastly more automated reconstruction; only millimetre-scale volumes have been done so far.

buildSteps.title: Record the living state
buildSteps.detail: A connectome alone is not a mind. You must record the ongoing activity and the strength of every synapse in a living, intact brain — currently impossible at that resolution without damaging the tissue.

buildSteps.title: Write down neuron and synapse rules
buildSteps.detail: Convert anatomy and recordings into equations for each cell type: how it sums inputs, fires, and changes its connections with use.

buildSteps.title: Build the emulation engine
buildSteps.detail: Distribute millions to billions of model neurons across many processors, with communication between them fine-grained enough to stay in biological time.

buildSteps.title: Validate against behaviour
buildSteps.detail: Run the model and compare its outputs with the animal it came from — the only practical test that the emulation is faithful rather than merely plausible.

buildSteps.title: Scale to a human brain
buildSteps.detail: A human cortex holds roughly 86 billion neurons and hundreds of trillions of synapses, requiring computing and memory far beyond today's machines.

buildSteps.title: Capture and transfer a living mind
buildSteps.detail: Ideally without destroying the original: high-resolution, non-destructive scanning plus a method to move the state onto the synthetic substrate. No route to this is known.

prerequisites.why: insect and small-animal circuits are mapped; a whole human brain has not been imaged at synapse resolution.

prerequisites.tech: Non-destructive in-vivo recording of all synapses
prerequisites.why: current methods either sample a tiny fraction of cells or require fixing and slicing the tissue.
large-scale brain simulations already run, but far slower than real time and at reduced detail.

prerequisites.tech: Validated models of learning and memory
prerequisites.why: plasticity rules are understood in fragments; no complete, tested account exists.

prerequisites.tech: A test for whether an emulation is the same person
prerequisites.why: there is no accepted scientific method to verify continuity of experience after a transfer, and the question may not be empirically decidable.

pathway.milestone: complete connectomes of insects and partial maps of mouse cortex (e.g. FlyWire 2024, MICrONS)
pathway.unlocks: testable models of real, if small, nervous systems.

pathway.milestone: behaviourally validated emulation of a small circuit, such as a fly's motion-detection pathway
pathway.unlocks: confidence that mapping plus simulation can reproduce function at all.

pathway.milestone: hybrid systems: brain tissue coupled to silicon, and neural prosthetics that replace damaged regions
pathway.unlocks: medical uses, and evidence that biological and synthetic processing can interoperate.

pathway.milestone: whole-brain emulation of a mammal at real time
pathway.unlocks: the first concrete test case for the idea.

pathway.milestone: gradual or scanning-based transfer of a human mind onto a non-biological substrate, with photonic or neuromorphic computing as one proposed host
pathway.unlocks: would raise questions of identity, consent and rights that science alone cannot answer.
